topic: Blind replicated continuous-treatment ADRF identification and qualitative honest simultaneous bands over a compatible nonempty fixed class. Under finite strata, compact dose support, a bounded structural response surface, Sobolev radii beta>1/2, overlap, and independent nonidentical asymmetric replicate errors with a uniform q_e>1 moment bound and possible open spectral zeros, prove analytic-cocycle identification of f_x, q_x, and mu(a)=sum_x P(X=x)q_x(a)/f_x(a). Construct finite-dimensional semi-infinite constrained-sieve and parallel exact-class bands with uniform simultaneous 1-alpha coverage, width at most 2B_Y, and uniformly o(1) expected maximal width. No finite decision algorithm, explicit O(r_n) rate, minimax match, or unconditional converse is claimed; the quantitative protected-cube inverse and fixed-nuisance Bernoulli packet remain open.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the minimax expected width of a uniformly honest simultaneous band for the ADRF over compact-support H^β latent-density and outcome-channel classes in blind two-replicate deconvolution with possibly band-limited errors, and is it exactly (log log n/log n)^(β-1/2)?

source_refs.claim: Proves matching compact-support minimax rates for latent-density estimation in L2 under unknown repeated-measure noise, but does not cover a marked outcome channel, sup norm, or confidence-band width.
source_refs.author: Jérémie Capitao-Miniconi, Elisabeth Gassiat, and Luc Lehéricy

source_refs.claim: Constructs uniform bands for nonparametric errors-in-variables regression, but the repeated-measurement case uses symmetry and conventional nonvanishing deconvolution.
source_refs.author: Kengo Kato and Yuya Sasaki

source_refs.claim: Provides linear expansions and pointwise inference for a deconvolution ADRF estimator, not an honest simultaneous band or an all-band expected-width converse.
source_refs.author: Wei Huang and Zheng Zhang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: Develops honest uniform confidence sets with expected-diameter guarantees for ill-posed models, but assumes a linear inverse operator rather than blind nonlinear characteristic-function factorization.
source_refs.author: Andrii Babii

source_refs.excerpt: an asymmetric Bernoulli exact-code subexperiment yields the matching lower bound over all honest measurable bands
Reuse the noise-only contour bank, reference-localized selector, and exact-code lower-bound construction

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing results divide the required argument among incompatible regimes: blind repeated-measure work supplies density L2 estimation and a Le Cam converse; errors-in-variables regression work supplies simultaneous bands under symmetry or nonvanishing transforms; ADRF work supplies pointwise inference with a known error law; and general honest inverse-problem bands assume a linear operator. The prior CausalSmith exact-code converse reduces to ordinary observed-dose regression and therefore does not survive latent-dose convolution. The missing lower-bound step is to hold a smooth positive f and admissible compact-spectrum errors fixed, perturb a valid Bernoulli mean 1/2+g(a), and prove both contiguity of the marked replicate laws and H^β-legal sup-norm separation of order T_n^(1/2-β). The matching upper step must control nonlinear confidence-set inversion for both characteristic-function channels and the ratio q/f.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A pair of theorems giving an empirical-characteristic-function confidence-set and constrained-analytic-sieve band with uniform coverage and maximal width O((log log n/log n)^(β-1/2)), together with a Le Cam or constrained-modulus converse showing every uniformly honest band has worst-case expected width Ω((log log n/log n)^(β-1/2)) using valid Bernoulli-outcome alternatives.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the closest causal estimand and nutrition-measurement-error motivation; its pointwise inferential endpoint can be sharpened into the need for whole-curve honesty under blind replicates.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Scientific conclusions concern an entire continuous dose-response curve -> the exposure is measured with substantial error -> existing ADRF deconvolution gives pointwise inference under known or nonvanishing error transforms -> blind replicated data require a rate-optimal honest simultaneous band and a matching impossibility result

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the constrained analytic polynomial estimator and compact-support Le Cam construction, replacing density L2 separation by a marked Bernoulli outcome-channel sup-norm modulus.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It generates the same logarithmic effective cutoff under the same blind replicate observation map; the first changed proof is precisely the marked outcome channel and H^β-to-L∞ separation.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its studentized supremum Gaussian approximation and multiplier-bootstrap proof, indexing the score by a feasible analytic characteristic-function confidence set instead of dividing by an estimated error transform.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly proves a simultaneous band for an outcome regression with a mismeasured regressor under a simpler inverse regime.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the testing-to-expected-length argument to frequency-localized Bernoulli alternatives after convolution.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested converse quantifies over every honest band, so it requires an expected-width lower bound rather than estimator-specific risk.

open_problems.open_problem: Does the analytic repeated-measurement factorization identify each stratum's outcome-weighted signed measure q_x, and hence the continuous-treatment ADRF, when the two unknown centered error laws are nonidentical and asymmetric and their characteristic functions have open zero sets?

source_refs.claim: Identifies and estimates a latent signal density from repeated measurements with unknown noise under coordinate independence, but treats an unmarked probability law rather than an outcome-weighted signed measure or causal ADRF.
source_refs.author: Jérémie Capitao-Miniconi, Elisabeth Gassiat, and Luc Lehéricy

source_refs.claim: Identifies and estimates a scalar error-contaminated ADRF, but its main model uses a known error characteristic function and Fourier inversion requiring nonvanishing.
source_refs.author: Wei Huang and Zheng Zhang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: Uses analytic continuation of a light-tailed signal transform for blind-deconvolution identification with unknown noise, but has no marked outcome channel or causal ratio target.
source_refs.author: Élisabeth Gassiat, Sylvain Le Corff, and Luc Lehéricy

source_refs.excerpt: Prove the exact learned-residual factorization and contour-identification identities

open_problems.why_unsolved: The probability-channel analytic argument normalizes a characteristic function at zero and can use positive-definiteness and unit mass. The outcome channel is the transform of the signed measure E[Y 1{A in da}|X=x], whose total mass is not fixed and whose transform need not be positive definite. The banked contour construction identifies a scalar coefficient after nuisance annihilation, not two latent measures from a two-dimensional blind factorization. The first new proof step is therefore a marked analytic-cocycle lemma establishing normalization and path-independence locally, compatibility of G_x with the probability-channel solution, and unique continuation of q_x across error-spectrum gaps without illicit division at zeros.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A law-level injectivity theorem with explicit local cocycle and marked-ratio recovery formulas for the entire transforms of f_x and q_x, analytic continuation across open error-spectrum zeros, Fourier recovery of both measures, and the resulting point-identification formula μ(a)=Σ_x P(X=x)q_x(a)/f_x(a) wherever f_x is bounded below.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest econometric formulation of an error-contaminated continuous-treatment ADRF and makes the causal target central before introducing deconvolution.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Continuous dose-response effects matter in observational health studies -> exposure measurement error invalidates error-free ADRF methods -> known-error deconvolution yields a weighted ADRF representation -> repeated unknown asymmetric errors with spectral gaps require marked analytic-cocycle identification

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its functional-equation and analytic-extension recovery of the latent transform from the joint repeated-measurement characteristic function, proving an additional compatibility lemma for the outcome-marked transform.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its observation map is the same blind two-replicate convolution map and compact support supplies the same entire-function source; q_x is the new signed object required by the resolution.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over empirical-characteristic-function regularization, deconvolution-regression linearization, and multiplier-bootstrap control for a supremum-indexed curve.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After cocycle identification, the ratio q_x/f_x is an errors-in-variables regression curve requiring simultaneous inverse-problem inference.

open_problems.open_problem: How does honest simultaneous inference for a blind replicated ADRF transition from the logarithmic point-identified regime to nonshrinking identification-robust sets when the near-origin characteristic-function modulus or its protected frequency radius deteriorates with n?

source_refs.claim: Constructs repeated-measurement density confidence bands robust to completeness or nonvanishing failure by inverting moment restrictions, but gives no shrinking-sequence rate phase diagram or outcome-ratio target.
source_refs.author: Kengo Kato, Yuya Sasaki, and Takuya Ura

source_refs.claim: Obtains blind point identification and minimax density estimation over fixed analytic signal and moment classes, leaving local-to-nonidentification sequences outside its fixed-class rate statement.
source_refs.author: Jérémie Capitao-Miniconi, Elisabeth Gassiat, and Luc Lehéricy

source_refs.claim: Shows in a general econometric topology that near nonidentification can make bounded confidence sets impossible, motivating a quantitative boundary for this inverse problem.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews and Anna Mikusheva

source_refs.excerpt: Leave the shrinking-separation phase diagram, adaptive switching, uniform inference, and matching local lower bounds
specifying a candidate phase boundary or a lower-bound construction for the Hölder-band loss

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fixed-class analytic continuation identifies through distant spectral gaps, whereas identification-robust moment inversion remains valid when completeness fails; neither literature quantifies the local sequence joining those endpoints. The prior spectral results also fix positive transform conditioning. When the near-origin lower modulus c_n or protected radius ν_n shrinks, empirical cocycle formation, analytic continuation, and marked-channel inversion may amplify noise at different rates, while q_x/f_x adds denominator amplification. The missing proof object is a sharp modulus linking observable characteristic-function conditioning to the analytic-sieve stability radius and a same-class lower experiment showing when this instability prevents any shrinking honest band.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform phase-transition theorem giving matching upper and lower expected sup-width rates R_n(c_n,ν_n,β,κ), with conditions for the fixed-class logarithmic rate, intermediate weak-identification rates, and nonvanishing diameter, plus a band whose coverage remains valid across those regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its identification-robust motivation explains why inference should not silently depend on completeness; the destination makes that concern quantitative for a causal curve.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Repeated-measurement identification often relies on fragile characteristic-function inversion -> nonvanishing or completeness may fail -> moment-restriction inversion preserves coverage under failure -> local transform strength should determine whether an ADRF band shrinks and at what rate

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt inversion of sieve moment restrictions with multiplier-bootstrap critical values so coverage survives weak or failed characteristic-function inversion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest repeated-measurement band construction explicitly robust to lack of completeness; the new result must add marked moments and sharp local-sequence diameter bounds.

method_exemplars.technique: Quantify the stability constants in analytic functional-equation recovery and match their deterioration with local alternatives.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its analytic blind identification supplies the strong-identification endpoint of the requested phase diagram.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt weak-, semi-strong-, and strong-identification asymptotics with critical values valid at drifting regime boundaries.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The cocycle's conditioning can drift between regular and effectively unidentified regimes, changing the relevant limit experiment.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one characterize a minimal cross-channel self-similarity or spectral-separation condition under which a single blind-replicate ADRF band is uniformly honest and rate-adaptive over β in a nontrivial interval, while proving adaptation impossible on the unrestricted union of H^β balls?

source_refs.claim: Provides adaptive density estimation for repeated measurements with unknown noise, but estimation adaptivity does not yield honest adaptive bands and the model has no outcome channel.
source_refs.author: Jérémie Capitao-Miniconi, Elisabeth Gassiat, and Luc Lehéricy

source_refs.claim: Proves honest adaptive bands over unrestricted nested Hölder balls are impossible and gives a distinguishability restriction restoring adaptation in direct density estimation.
source_refs.author: Marc Hoffmann and Richard Nickl

source_refs.claim: Shows self-similarity is necessary and sufficient for honest adaptive bands in direct density, regression, and white-noise models, not for blind nonlinear inverse recovery or a ratio-valued causal curve.
source_refs.author: Adam D. Bull

source_refs.excerpt: Unknown-smoothness adaptation, boundary bands, multivariate modifiers, and weak separation remain outside

open_problems.why_unsolved: Adaptive point estimation in blind deconvolution conflicts with the classical impossibility of honest band adaptation over unrestricted smoothness unions. Direct-model self-similarity is insufficient here because distinguishability can be lost separately in f_x or the signed outcome measure q_x, while cancellation in q_x/f_x can make the ADRF smoother than either channel. The first unresolved step is to define an observable-scale cross-channel separation condition after convolution and analytic continuation, compute its logarithmic testing radius, and show that data-driven cutoff selection preserves simultaneous coverage rather than merely estimator risk.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient adaptation theorem specifying a self-similar or spectrally separated subclass of pairs (f_x,q_x), constructing one uniformly honest band attaining (log log n/log n)^(β-1/2) for every β in a stated interval, and proving a testing lower bound excluding honest adaptation over the unrestricted union.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly separates estimator adaptivity from honest-band adaptivity and explains why a structural self-similarity condition is the price of adaptation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Smoothness is unknown -> adaptive estimators exist -> honest adaptive bands are impossible on unrestricted smoothness classes -> identify the minimal cross-channel condition that restores adaptation for blind ADRF inference

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the reduction of honest adaptation to testing between nested smoothness classes, measuring separation after the repeated-measurement forward map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested resolution is an if-and-only-if adaptation frontier, with direct-model distinguishability replaced by marked blind-deconvolution distinguishability.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt multiscale self-similarity bias detection and band calibration to analytically continued Fourier coefficients of both f_x and q_x.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the canonical constructive argument showing that self-similarity restores honest adaptive sup bands.

method_exemplars.technique: Use its adaptive analytic polynomial sieve as the band center and add a data-driven bias envelope certified by cross-channel self-similarity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already adapts an estimator in the same blind repeated-measurement experiment; the changed step is honest bias certification for the causal ratio.

literature_map:
Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat & Lehéricy (EJS 2025, arXiv:2409.02014) is the closest anchor: blind repeated-measure density identification, analytic estimation, adaptivity, and a compact-support minimax L2 converse.
Gassiat, Le Corff & Lehéricy (AoS 2022, arXiv:2006.14226) supplies the broader multivariate analytic-continuation identification template with wholly unknown noise.
Huang & Zhang (JRSSB 2023, arXiv:2211.04642) is the closest causal-target paper: error-contaminated continuous-treatment ADRF, deconvolution estimation, and pointwise asymptotics.
Its main analysis assumes a known, everywhere-nonzero error characteristic function; repeated unknown errors are discussed as a plug-in route rather than analyzed under asymmetric spectral gaps.
Kato & Sasaki (JoE 2019, arXiv:1702.03377) prove uniform errors-in-variables regression bands by multiplier bootstrap, but their replicate route uses symmetry and conventional characteristic-function inversion.
Kato & Sasaki (JoE 2018, arXiv:1608.02251) give unknown-error deconvolution density bands from auxiliary or symmetric-panel information under nonvanishing ordinary- or supersmooth errors.
Kato, Sasaki & Ura (QE 2021, arXiv:1808.09375) avoid completeness by inverting linearized Kotlarski moment restrictions, yielding uniform-size density bands and fixed-alternative consistency rather than sharp shrinking widths.
Babii (Econometric Theory 2020, arXiv:1611.03015) gives honest confidence sets and expected-diameter control for ill-posed models, but the operator is linear rather than a blind nonlinear characteristic-function factorization.
Delaigle, Hall & Meister (AoS 2008, arXiv:0804.0713) show replicated-data density and regression estimators can match known-error first-order performance under the classical symmetric setup.
Comte & Kappus (JMVA 2015, arXiv:1407.3495) remove symmetry for repeated-measure density estimation but retain standard spectral regularity and do not address outcome bands.
Hall & Meister (AoS 2007, DOI:10.1214/009053607000000028) and Belomestny & Goldenshluger (AoS 2021, arXiv:1907.11024) handle known error transforms with zeros, separating the zeros issue from blindness.
Hoffmann & Nickl (AoS 2011, arXiv:1202.5145) and Bull (EJS 2012, arXiv:1110.4985) show why adaptive estimation does not imply honest adaptive bands and identify distinguishability or self-similarity as the missing condition.
